cefrAlignment: Matches B2 spoken production ('can develop a clear argument, supporting points of view with subsidiary points and relevant examples') and B2 interaction (polite partial agreement/disagreement); models use B2 range without C1-only structures.
examFidelity: TOEFL Take an Interview (no prep, 45 s) and TOEIC Express an opinion (45 s prep, 60 s) timings match exams.ts; models now fit those limits at a natural pace and the TOEIC tip no longer assumes note-taking is permitted.
fixes: Trimmed the TOEFL interview model from 120 to 100 words (it needed about 160 wpm to fit 45 s) and changed its opening from 'I agree up to a point' (nothing had been stated to agree with) to 'It's a good idea up to a point'; updated the target phrase to match
Trimmed the TOEIC practice model from 135 to 130 words and fixed the illogical ending 'But overall, that's why I'd say…' that followed a concession
Trimmed the TOEIC model audio from 144 to 130 words so it fits 60 s at a natural pace; tidied 'it wouldn't work for every job, like nurses' and updated the walkthrough quote

TOEIC tip: 'write key words' changed to 'plan key words' (note-taking in TOEIC Speaking could not be verified) and the unsupported 'raters reward…' claim reworded around ETS's published criteria (relevance and completeness of content as well as language)
Walkthrough: 'only needs to note' changed to 'only needs to plan a few key words'
openConcerns: Model audio is browser TTS; a human recording would model natural pausing and emphasis much better for an opinion task
Whether notes may be written during TOEIC Speaking preparation could not be confirmed from an official source; advice is worded neutrally ('plan')
learnerOutcome: A learner can open a 45–60 second answer with a clear position, support it with one or two reasons and a specific example, acknowledge the other side, and finish with a conclusion inside the TOEFL/TOEIC time limit.
